name: Camping 101: Mining

angles.text: As a miner, you learn to shape earth and ore into a lodestone that anchors a wilderness camp.
As a cook, you learn the firecraft a camp needs from cooking trainers.

faq.answer: A lodestone anchors a campsite in the wilderness.
faq.q: What is a lodestone used for?

faq.answer: Townspeople and settlement authorities frown on tents in public squares and streets. Set up camp beyond the town limits.
faq.q: Can I set up camp inside a town or city?

faq.answer: A camp needs a warm fire burning nearby.
faq.q: What is required before setting up a camp?

faq.answer: Cooking instructors and chefs across Azeroth teach the basic fire-starting skills used in cooking.
faq.q: Where do I learn how to build a campfire?

faq.answer: Mining teaches you to work the minerals and stone needed to make a lodestone.
faq.q: How does mining connect to crafting a lodestone?

faq.answer: Go beyond the city gates into the open wilderness, where you can find room to camp away from townsfolk.
faq.q: Where should I go to test my new camp?

sections.body: Beyond guarded roads, a miner must rely on fieldcraft. Mineral knowledge gives you the means to shape a lodestone, the anchor for a campsite in the wild.
sections.title: Fieldcraft for Miners

sections.body: A campsite belongs beyond town limits, where travelers can pitch their shelters without troubling settled folk. Choose a place in the open wilds. A camp also needs a fire to ward off the night chill. Learning to build one is part of the same fieldcraft as working stone.
sections.title: Rules of the Wild

summary: Out beyond the guarded roads, miners learn to make a lodestone for a wilderness camp. The work pairs knowledge of stone with the firecraft needed to live outdoors.
